citation: Anwer RW, Abrar M, Ullah M, Salam A, Ullah F. Advanced intrusion detection in the industrial Internet of Things using federated learning and LSTM models. Ad Hoc Networks 178:103991, 2025. doi:10.1016/j.adhoc.2025.103991

A1.evidence: Sec 3.8: "A standard 80:10:10 split was used for training, validation, and testing" - random/stratified/temporal not stated.

A2.evidence: CNN-Bi-LSTM "to capture temporal dependencies"; "Bi-LSTM networks are beneficial for analyzing sequential data"; no windows, timesteps or input shape described.

A3.evidence: Sec 3.2: min-max scaling "Each feature xi is transformed into the range [0,1]" and SMOTE; fit set and order relative to the split not stated.

A4.evidence: Sec 3.8: "50 communication rounds"; "Training was carried out over 50 epochs, with early stopping" - local epochs per round (E in Algorithm 1) not specified.

A5.evidence: No statement that the centralized and FL variants use the same budget (Sec 3.8).

A6.evidence: Only centralized vs FL versions of the authors' own model (Table 3); no external methods or literature numbers.

A7.evidence: Sec 3.7: "accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Area Under the Curve (AUC)" plus TPR/FPR; no MCC/balanced accuracy.

A8.evidence: "training was distributed across multiple clients"; number of clients and partition not described.

A9.evidence: No repeated runs, std or statistical test reported.

A10.evidence: X-IIoTID, WUSTL-IIoT, Edge-IIoTset each evaluated on its own 80:10:10 split; no cross-dataset test.

A11.evidence: No code link or availability statement.

notes: The only comparison is centralized vs federated versions of the same model, coded rerun (as the screening accepted it as a baseline). If windows are later confirmed, A2 would depend on the unspecified split type.
